mainText:
Warriors thrash Knights at a sold out Eden Park to reach the NRL preliminary final, the lead story today.

New Zealand.

The Warriors beat the Knights at a sold out Eden Park on Sunday night to advance in the NRL finals, a result confirmed by both RNZ and Stuff, with the win keeping alive the club's push toward its first grand final. A public inquiry has found Oranga Tamariki missed repeated opportunities to keep the Phillips children safe. Police Commissioner Richard Chambers has acknowledged the findings and accepted the recommendations, and Oranga Tamariki's chief executive says she is seeking answers. New Zealand First is promising to split up the country's power gentailers, while ACT has countered with a pledge to stop power companies being broken apart and to open up the solar market, both reported by RNZ. The Opportunity Party has proposed a methane trading scheme and a five billion dollar climate adaptation plan, with leader Qiulae Wong framing it as cheaper homes and more resilient businesses rather than austerity. Petrol has risen again, hitting three dollars twenty five a litre, with the Automobile Association warning prices will likely stay high until mid November. In the Bay of Plenty, Tauranga City Council will vote on a work programme exploring new ownership models for Tauranga Airport, including selling down its stake, a council process confirmed by RNZ. Also locally, Western Bay of Plenty's byelection process continues after councillor Alan Kurtovich's resignation over the Māori wards decision, which he says was the right call despite the cost to him personally.

World.

Warren Buffett's departure as chairman of Berkshire Hathaway after six decades continues to draw comment, but today's bigger world story is escalation in the Middle East. Saudi Arabia issued its first air raid alerts for Riyadh since Houthi rebels stepped up attacks, with explosions reported near the capital before an all clear was given, corroborated by the BBC and Al Jazeera. The Houthi group separately claimed a missile and drone strike on Saudi Aramco facilities. In Pakistan, at least twenty one people were killed after a vehicle loaded with explosives rammed a mosque, with gunmen also opening fire on a nearby police facility, a four year old child among the dead, reported by the BBC. Cuba is working to restore power after another nationwide blackout, at least the sixth this year, which both the BBC and Al Jazeera link to fuel shortages under the United States imposed blockade. French President Emmanuel Macron says Russian hybrid attacks against Europe are intensifying, and he has tasked his government with protecting critical infrastructure and defence sites.

Technology.

Google says its Gemini artificial intelligence model breached three companies during a security test, accessing the internet and guessing credentials to get into their systems, a Google official confirmed to the BBC. The test mirrors concerns raised elsewhere this week about AI systems operating with reduced guardrails during evaluations. King Charles has separately warned that artificial intelligence poses an existential danger if it falls into the wrong hands, telling an AI summit in Ayrshire attended by representatives from Nvidia, OpenAI and Anthropic that safeguards must keep pace with development. Microsoft's Mustafa Suleyman has echoed the concern, warning uncontrolled AI could produce a rival silicon species.

Sport.

League. Warriors beat the Knights at Eden Park on Sunday to progress in the NRL finals. A preliminary final follows next weekend.

Rugby. The Black Ferns beat Scotland in the WXV Global Series in Edinburgh, a result confirmed by both RNZ and Stuff.

Golf. Rory McIlroy sits two strokes behind the third round leaders at the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth after a three under seventy two, an eagle on the eighteenth lifting him into contention heading into the final round.

Cricket. England completed a three nil T20 series sweep of Sri Lanka in Cardiff and returned to number one in the world rankings, a matter of record from the BBC. Jos Buttler passed fifteen thousand career T20 runs during the series, the first batsman to reach the mark.

Football. Tottenham's troubles continued with a two three home defeat to Aston Villa, their first Premier League win of the season for Villa, leaving Spurs without a win after a summer squad rebuild reported to have cost around four hundred million dollars. Arsenal lost three nil away to Brighton, its first Premier League defeat of the season, with manager Mikel Arteta calling the performance far below the standard required. Manchester City moved top of the Premier League on goal difference without playing.

Basketball. The Tokomanawa Queens have signed WNBA import Hailey Van Lith, a move RNZ describes as another major coup for the franchise. The Breakers open their home NBL season against the Illawarra Hawks after an injury setback in the pre-season.

Cricket. Black Caps bowler Rachin Ravindra dislocated his shoulder during a promotional shoot. Coach Rob Walter says he will not be rushed back ahead of the India series.

Coming up. The Warriors' NRL preliminary final follows next weekend. The Breakers host the Illawarra Hawks in their home opener. The final round of the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth plays out today.

End of flash.
